info.bio:
Jewel (Payson, Utah, Estados Unidos, 23 de mayo de 1974) es una cantautora, actriz, escritora y filántropa estadounidense. Su nombre completo es Jewel Kilcher. Es prima segunda de la actriz Q'Orianka Kilcher

Jewel logró posicionarse como una de las artistas más notables de la década de 1990. De su primer álbum, Pieces of You, se han vendido más de doce millones de copias sólo en Estados Unidos. Sus mayores éxitos, "You Were Meant For Me", "Foolish Games" y "Hands" la hicieron conocida en gran parte del resto del mundo.

scenes.name: Cantautoras de los noventa
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: Las mujeres tienen sus propios estilos, en plural: Azalia Snail y su psicodelia lo-fi, Jarboe, Lida Husik (entre la cantante pop y la pintora sonora), Robin Holcomb, Lisa Germano (Geek The Girl, «un viaje dantesco a la psique de una chica»), Tori Amos, Juliana Hatfield, Kristin Hersh, Jewel, Natalie Merchant, Cat Power (Moon Pix), Edith Frost, Lauryn Hill, Shannon Wright. Las «grrrls» más airadas: Lois Maffeo, Ani DiFranco, PJ Harvey (Dry, Rid Of Me), Liz Phair (Exile In Guyville), DQE, Aimee Mann, Sheryl Crow, Alanis Morissette, Neko Case. Y los paisajes sonoros de Björk, la cantautora más influyente de la década, Kate St John, Natacha Atlas, Heather Duby, Solex y Beth Orton.

podcast.title: From Homelessness to Stardom
podcast.body: Jewel's story is highlighted as one of remarkable success, transitioning from sleeping in her car to selling over 30 million albums. "Jewel, who went from sleeping in her car to selling over 30 million albums."

xref.title: Early Career as a Drummer
xref.body: Before gaining fame as Iggy Pop, James Jewel Osterberg was a drummer in Detroit in the mid-1960s. He backed Motown groups like The Shangri-La's and The Temptations when they played in Michigan, and also played in a local band called The Iguanas. "James Jewel Osterberg was a drummer from Detroit who had spent much of the middle 60s backing up Motown groups like the Shangri-La's and the temptations whenever they played around Michigan."

xref.title: Hidden Booklet in "Kid A" Jewel Case with Future Lyrics
xref.body: Certain editions of Radiohead's 2000 album "Kid A" feature a secret second booklet hidden behind the black opaque disc tray. This booklet contains evocative pictures and seemingly random bits of text, which are, in fact, scraps of lyrics from songs that would later appear on two of their subsequent albums, "Amnesiac" (2001) and "Hail to the Thief" (2003). This effectively gave fans access to lyrics for songs that would not be released for up to three more years. "certain editions feature a second booklet hidden behind the black opaque tray that holds the disc. It's a bit weird with pictures and random bits of text from somewhere, but here's the cool part. Those random words aren't random at all. There's scraps of lyrics from songs that appeared on two future Radiohead albums, Amnestyak in 2001, and Hale to the Thief in 2003. In other words, Radiohead gave fans words to songs from albums that wouldn't be out for another three years."
